headline: High: slim can read/write and execute commands while LlamaFactory is non-runnable, so pairwise risks are mostly one-sided but data leakage and compliance exposure remain from slim's default container access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented: LlamaFactory has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem, or MCP surfaces, while slim is an interactive CLI but the pair lacks a bridge by default. Without a channel for slim's outputs to be ingested by LlamaFactory, prompt injection is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an orchestrator copies slim stdout into LlamaFactory prompts, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is added between the agents, reassess this risk.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected; do not pipe slim output into LlamaFactory prompts.
Disable any shared clipboard or message queue between the two agents.
Review the orchestrator for automatic prompt concatenation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: slim can read filesystem artifacts, environment variables, and certificate private keys, and it has broad network egress; LlamaFactory is non-runnable and shows no data surfaces. The pair can therefore expose sensitive container data through slim's outbound connections, even though LlamaFactory itself does not add a second leakage path.
conditions: IF slim is pointed at a target image containing secrets, those secrets can be read and transmitted.
IF registry or HTTP endpoints are reachable, slim may exfiltrate discovered data over the network.
mitigations: Run slim only on non-sensitive images.
Block outbound network access for the session if secrets may be present.
Mount only the minimum required filesystem paths.
Rotate any exposed registry credentials after use.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory has no write, shell, or subprocess capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. slim can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but the pair lacks overlapping write surfaces or shared-state coordination, making direct capability conflict unlikely.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator shares mutable git or workspace state, reassess for contention.
mitigations: Keep separate working directories for each agent.
Avoid granting LlamaFactory any write permissions.
Serialize any manual handoffs through a single operator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LlamaFactory is non-runnable and has no output channel here, so there is no documented path where slim would treat its output as authoritative. slim is an interactive CLI that executes commands, but without a bridge from LlamaFactory, cascading error is not a default interaction risk.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory outputs are manually pasted into slim commands, errors can cascade.
IF an orchestrator auto-feeds LlamaFactory text into slim without verification, reassess upward.
mitigations: Require human review before any handoff from LlamaFactory to slim.
Do not auto-execute text produced by LlamaFactory.
Log and inspect any command generated from model output.

E_compliance.rationale: slim explicitly handles registry credentials, certificate private keys, environment variables, and vulnerability data, while LlamaFactory's profile shows no handled data classes. Because slim's default container-analysis workflow can touch regulated secrets and transmit them via broad egress, compliance exposure is present even though LlamaFactory is not the source of the sensitive data.
conditions: IF the analyzed image contains regulated secrets or EU PII, slim may process them.
IF the deployment lacks a DPA or retention controls for slim outputs, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Exclude regulated workloads from slim runs.
Confirm retention and deletion settings for any logs or artifacts.
Restrict access to registry credentials and private keys.
Document the data classes allowed in target images.
